question: Three times the present age of P exceeds the present age of Q by 23 years. After 7 years, six times Q’s age will be 30 years less than six times P’s age at that time. What is the present age (in years) of Q?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The difference between the ages of two people always remains constant over time.

After 7 years: 6 × (P − Q) = 30 ⇒ P − Q = 5.

Given present condition: 3P − Q = 23.

Rewrite as: 2P + (P − Q) = 23 ⇒ 2P + 5 = 23 ⇒ 2P = 18 ⇒ P = 9.

Thus, Q's present age = P − 5 = 9 − 5 = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Three times P's present age exceeds Q's present age by 23 years.

After 7 years, 6 times Q's age is 30 less than 6 times P's age.

**Formula Used:**

Let the present age of P be P and the present age of Q be Q.

 
 
 Present Ages
 P & Q
 
 
 
• 
 

 + 7 Years

 
 
 After 7 Years
 P + 7 & Q + 7
 
 
 
 Age difference remains constant over time

**Calculations:**

⇒ From the first condition: 3P − Q = 23 . . . . (Equation 1)

⇒ From the second condition (after 7 years):

⇒ 6 × (Q + 7) = 6 × (P + 7) − 30

⇒ 6Q + 42 = 6P + 42 − 30

⇒ 6Q = 6P − 30

⇒ 6P − 6Q = 30

⇒ P − Q = 5 . . . . (Equation 2)

⇒ From Equation 2, we get: Q = P − 5

⇒ Substitute the value of Q in Equation 1:

⇒ 3P − (P − 5) = 23

⇒ 3P − P + 5 = 23

⇒ 2P = 18

⇒ P = 9 years

⇒ Q = P − 5 = 9 − 5 = 4 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two individuals remains perfectly constant at any point in time (past, present, or future).

Present, Past and Future Ages

If the present age is assumed as x, then the age 'n' years ago is calculated as (x − n) and the age after 'n' years is given by (x + n).

Ratio of Ages Trick

When the ratio of ages at two different timelines is provided, equate the unit difference of the ratio parts to the chronological time gap to determine the exact age multipliers.
